item.title: C++ AVX __m256 Pointer Aliasing Safety and Alternatives
item.description:
“C++ AVX __m256 Pointer Aliasing Safety and Alternatives”

When dealing with Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX) in C++ through Intel intrinsics, a common point of confusion arises around pointer aliasing, specifically when interacting with the __m256, __m256i, and __m256d vector types. Is it permissible, and does it yield optimal code, to directly dereference a pointer to these types, or must one strictly adhere to using intrinsic load/store functions like _mm256_load_ps()?

Direct Dereferencing of __m256* Pointers

The core issue revolves around the strict aliasing rules of the ISO C++ standard, which typically forbid accessing an object through a pointer of an incompatible type (leading to Undefined Behavior, or UB).

item.title: Efficiently Convert Integers to Hexadecimal Strings in Assembly & SIMD
item.description:
“Efficiently Convert Integers to Hexadecimal Strings in Assembly & SIMD”

Converting integers to their hexadecimal string representations is a common task in programming, often requiring efficient implementations for performance-critical applications. This involves processing each 4-bit segment (nibble) of an integer and mapping it to its corresponding ASCII hexadecimal character. Several approaches exist, ranging from traditional assembly loops to leveraging modern SIMD (Single Instruction, Multiple Data) extensions for parallel processing.

Core Logic: Nibble Extraction and Mapping

The fundamental principle behind integer-to-hexadecimal conversion is extracting each nibble (4 bits) of the integer and converting it into an ASCII character. Since hexadecimal is base-16, each digit represents 4 bits.

item.title: Efficient Horizontal Vector Summation Techniques Explained
item.description:
“Efficient Horizontal Vector Summation Techniques Explained”

When working with Single Instruction, Multiple Data (SIMD) instructions, a common operation is the horizontal reduction, such as summing all elements within a vector. This process allows for efficient aggregation of data, particularly in performance-critical applications like scientific computing, signal processing, and machine learning. This post delves into various strategies for achieving efficient horizontal vector summation across different SIMD instruction sets and data types.
